# Truncation of an arbitrary concave sequence with its peak-block correction

This is an application of the already proved moment theorems in
`candidate efcef1959b4a9d5f` and
`candidate 273393b2aa6803aa`, retaining their
peak-index coefficient. It is not a new independent moment theorem.

Let f_0,...,f_(L-1) be a nonnegative, nonzero concave sequence, L>=1.
Let R=max_i f_i>0 and fix ANY peak index j with f_j=R. Define

    Q_p(c)=sum_i (f_i-c)_+^p,      0<=c<=R.

For 0<=t<R, its strictly positive superlevel indices form an interval
[a(t),b(t)] of integer indices containing j. Put

    kappa_j(t)=1/2 [1/(2(j-a(t))+1)
                        +1/(2(b(t)-j)+1)].      (1)

For every REAL p>=2 and 0<=c<R,

    Q_p(c) >= (1-c/R)^(p+1) Q_p(0)
       +(R-c)^(p+1) integral_0^c
                          kappa_j(t)/(R-t)^2 dt. (2)

In particular kappa_j is nondecreasing, is at least 1/L, and

    Q_p(c) >= (1-c/R)^(p+1) Q_p(0)
                         +kappa_j(0)c(R-c)^p/R. (3)

Both formulas include zero endpoint values and arbitrary peak plateaus.
At c=R the corresponding statement is checked directly with all terms
zero, using the explicit remainder in (3), or the continuous limit of
the remainder in (2). The inequality without any remainder is strict
when 0<c<R. If L=1, (2) and (3) are identities.

## Proof

Superlevel indices of a concave sequence are consecutive: if two
values exceed t, each intermediate value is at least their positive
linear interpolant and also exceeds t. As t rises, a(t) can only
increase and b(t) can only decrease; this proves monotonicity of
kappa_j(t). The harmonic-mean inequality gives

    kappa_j(t)>=1/[b(t)-a(t)+1]>=1/L.            (4)

The archived quadratic inequality, applied to a sequence g with
maximum H at relative peak index k and length m, says exactly

    3 sum g_i^2-2H sum g_i
        >=H^2/2 [1/(2k+1)+1/(2(m-1-k)+1)].     (5)

Its proof applies separately on the two sides of the chosen peak
and subtracts the repeated peak term. It permits either side to
have length zero and does not require a unique maximum.

We record how its peak coefficient survives the archived level
integration argument. Suppose g has maximum H and fixed peak
coefficient kappa. Every positive truncation (g_i-t)_+ has a
shorter block with the SAME chosen peak and coefficient at least
kappa, by the monotonicity just proved. Normalize H=1. For p>2,
multiply (5) for this truncated block by t^(p-3) and integrate
from 0 to 1. With A=sum g_i^p, B=sum g_i^(p-1), elementary power
integration gives

    integral_0^1 t^(p-3)[3sum(g_i-t)_+^2
                    -2(1-t)sum(g_i-t)_+]dt
         =2[(p+1)A-pB]/[(p-2)(p-1)p].

The integrated lower bound is
2kappa/[(p-2)(p-1)p]. All sums are finite, the endpoint
power is integrable for p>2, and adjoining zero terms occurs
only AFTER (5) is applied on the actual positive block. Hence

    (p+1)sum g_i^p-pH sum g_i^(p-1)
                                      >=kappa H^p. (6)

For p=2 this is already (5). Thus (6) is precisely the archived
moment argument with its stronger peak coefficient retained.

Now fix c<R, put h=R-c, and apply (6) to the positive block
g_i=f_i-c. Its maximum is h and its coefficient is kappa_j(c).
For p>=2 the function Q_p is continuously differentiable at
every truncation knot, with derivative

    Q_p'(c)=-p sum_i (f_i-c)_+^(p-1).

Therefore F_p(c)=Q_p(c)/(R-c)^(p+1) satisfies

    F_p'(c)
      =[(p+1)Q_p(c)-p(R-c)Q_(p-1)(c)]/(R-c)^(p+2)
      >=kappa_j(c)/(R-c)^2.                     (7)

All positive-part powers in the derivative have positive exponent.
Zero endpoint values and terms exactly equal to c contribute zero.
The chosen maximum index remains in the positive block for every
c<R, so (7) also includes knots at repeated nonmaximum values.
Integrating (7) over [0,c] gives (2). Monotonicity of kappa_j
and integration of 1/(R-t)^2 give (3).

The remainder of (2) is an EXACT FINITE KNOT SUM. Let
0=t_0<t_1<...<t_m=c be all distinct sequence values lying
strictly between 0 and c, together with 0 and c. On each open
interval (t_l,t_(l+1)) choose any s_l and let k_l=kappa_j(s_l).
Then the integral in (2) is exactly

    sum_(l=0)^(m-1) k_l
                     [1/(R-t_(l+1))-1/(R-t_l)]. (8)

Changing finitely many endpoint values of the step function does
not change this integral. Also 0<kappa_j(t)<=1, so its remainder
in (2) is bounded above by c(R-c)^p/R, which tends to zero as
c increases to R. This justifies the stated continuous endpoint
extension without asserting integrability up to R itself.

The symmetric sequence of length 2N+1 has j=N and
kappa_j(0)>=1/(2N+1), recovering the strengthened symmetric
truncation formula. For p=1 the corresponding universal assertion
fails, with exact examples in
`candidate 888842a3bcf9aa99`.
